transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Time: 16:00 - 16:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Owen Brooks (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Jenna Li (Portside Head of Search), Mark Alvarez (Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Data Scientist), Ethan Park (SRE)

Auto summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embedding generation and reranker chaining. Customer asked about data retention, VPC, and perf on 5-50 token queries.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Uh, nice to meet you all. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Jenna: Hi, Jenna here. Head of Search at Portside.
[00:14] Mark: Mark Alvarez — engineering, lead.
[00:18] Priya: Priya Singh, data science.
[00:21] Ethan: Ethan Park, SRE.
[00:24] Owen: Owen Brooks, solutions engineering for Redwood. Samir on mute but on the call.
[00:30] Maya: Cool, the agenda today — short demo of the hosted embeddings API, show how the reranker endpoint plugs in, quick Console tour and then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Jenna: Yep, perfect.
[00:42] Mark: Sounds good.

[01:12] Owen: Alright I'll share my screen. Um, first thing — embeddings are simple calls to /v1/embeddings, we return a float vector, length depends on model. For search folks the typical pattern is store vectors in your vector DB then run a similarity query and optionally call our reranker for top-K.
[01:35] Priya: Quick question, are the vectors deterministic? We need stable hashes for incremental indexing.
[01:41] Owen: Good question. Deterministic per model version — if you change the model or quantization profile you'll get differences. We recommend pinning model versions in config. There's also a reclaimable seed param but it's not usually needed.

[02:05] Maya: I'll jump in with a customer example — one of our retail customers runs embeddings for a 100M doc corpus, they use hosted API for embedding generation and Redwood Console to monitor token costs. For rerank they call /v1/rerank which accepts the query, candidate docs and returns scores and an ordered list.
[02:30] Mark: Is the reranking running on the same model infra or is it a separate service?
[02:34] Owen: Typically it's the same serving runtime with different model configs; you can choose a lighter embedding model for candidate generation and a heavier reranker for scoring. The runtime handles batching & KV cache across these calls. Sometimes the transcript engine mislabels KV-cache as K-V — we've seen that in ops notes.

[03:05] Ethan: We're worried about latency — our SLAs are 200ms p50 for search. Can you hit that with hosted?
[03:12] Owen: Depends on query complexity and model. For small candidates (K=10) and a light reranker we routinely hit sub-100ms p50 in hosted for US regions. If you need predictable p95/p99 then Dedicated helps — reserved pools reduce jitter.

[04:00] Priya: What about cost math? We run about 10M searches/month. Any ballpark?
[04:06] Maya: We'll send an explicit cost model, but rough rule: embeddings for indexing is a one-time cost; online queries cost depends on candidate generation (vector DB retrieval) plus rerank token cost. Our Optimize tool can simulate batching to reduce per-token fees.

[04:38] Owen: Let me demo a live flow — creating an embedding then a rerank call. (screen) Here's the API payload for embeddings — text, model: redwood-embed-medium, metadata optional. We return vector length 1536, odd decimals, noise etc.
[05:05] Owen: Now candidate generation — we mock up a top-50 from the vector DB and call /v1/rerank with query, candidates (title + snippet). The reranker returns normalized scores and a final order. You can request explain which returns per-document logits but note explain increases cost and latency.

[06:00] Jenna: Is the explain output safe for PII? We don't want model outputs echoed back.
[06:06] Owen: Explain is de‑identified token-level info, but good call — if you have strict PII rules we recommend returning only scores and an ID; don't return model generated spans. Also we can strip or redact in the Console.

[07:10] Samir: Quick Console peek — in the Console you can see per-route latency, per-model token breakdown, sample queries, and retrain/rollout controls. Here's a rerank route with a canary at 10% to compare a smaller model vs bigger model.
[07:39] Mark: Nice — do you have an audit log for who called what? We need that for compliance.
[07:44] Samir: Yes — audit logs with SSO identity, request payload hashes, response codes; retained per your plan. For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS and on-prem audit sinks.

[08:25] Priya: About data residency — some manifests need to stay in EU, are there region pinning options?
[08:31] Owen: Hosted regional controls are available; we also offer Private VPC deployments if you need complete on-prem or region-locked hosting. That path includes RBAC and HSM integrations.

[09:10] Jenna: Security paper checklist: SOC2, ISO27001, SSO/SAML, KMS, encryption at rest, data deletion policy.
[09:18] Owen: We'll attach our SOC2 report and a short security whitepaper. For KMS we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys.

[10:00] Maya: Switching to a small demo scenario — Priya you shared a 10k doc sample earlier?
[10:06] Priya: Yes uploaded to the Share link, you should have access.
[10:10] Owen: Great — we'll run a 1k piece test. (typing) Starting embedding ingest into a test workspace... note that ingestion parallelism is adjustable to balance cost and time.

[11:05] Priya: While that runs, can you explain batching? I.e., how do we avoid high per-token cost on many concurrent user queries?
[11:12] Owen: Continuous batching in the runtime aggregates requests within a very short window (ms) to amortize kernel cost — but there's a latency tradeoff. Optimize suggests optimal batch sizes and timeout thresholds based on your QPS pattern.

[12:00] Mark: If we go with hosted but later want Dedicated, how disruptive is the migration?
[12:07] Maya: Not very — the API surface is the same. You can pin model versions and route to dedicated pools via configuration; traffic switch is a config change plus canary. We handle model artifacts transfer if needed.

[13:20] Ethan: Networking question — do we need to open inbound ports? We're sensitive about public endpoints.
[13:26] Owen: Hosted uses outbound TLS to Redwood; no inbound. For Private you deploy inside your VPC, so you control ingress. We'll send a network diagram.

[14:30] Owen: The rerank response payload example — shows id, score, explanation (optional). Note occasional transcription in our demo notes calls the rerank endpoint 're-ranker' spelled different, sorry for the noise on the docs.

[15:05] Priya: Are embeddings stable across model quantization? We plan to quantize to save storage.
[15:12] Owen: Quantization can shift vectors; we recommend keeping a mapping: index vectors in original float format then use quantized variants for low-latency lookup, or re-embed on major model changes. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.

[16:10] Maya: Let's run a quick interactive test — I'll query "where is shipment 4392" against the test shard and show rerank differences between small and medium reranker.
[16:20] (demo runs)
[17:00] Jenna: We can see the medium model pushes better recall on entity-rich queries, but latency jumps ~40ms, close to p95 threshold for us.
[17:10] Owen: Exactly — tradeoff. You can set automatic fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical reads. Redwood routing policies let you route by latency target or cost budget.

[18:00] Mark: Any real-world numbers for p95 on heavy rerankers?
[18:06] Owen: With K=10, p95 for medium reranker in hosted US-West was ~230ms in our internal bench on a mixed-power machine — your numbers may vary; we'll run a bench on your 10k sample.

[19:15] Priya: On the bench — can we measure quality like MRR/ndcg?
[19:20] Owen: Yes, we can instrument eval harnesses and compute MRR, NDCG, and create regression alerts in Console if scores dip after model updates.

[20:00] Maya: Time to talk about next steps — interested in a quick POC: Redwood runs a 10k doc benchmark against your queries, measure latency/cost/ndcg, then we propose configuration. Is that right?
[20:12] Jenna: That's the plan. We want a tight scope: 10k docs, 500 representative queries, measure p50/p95 and ndcg; also demonstrate SOC2 docs and a region mapping.

[21:05] Owen: I'll own the benchmark with Priya and Samir — we'll need a short spec from you: data format, query set, expected metrics.

[22:00] (background cross talk)
[22:30] Priya: One more thing — our compliance team will ask about retention and deletion URLs. How long do you keep logs?
[22:38] Samir: Default logs retained 30 days, but enterprise plans can extend or forward logs into your SIEM. For deletion we support on-demand scrubbing and a purge API.

[23:15] Ethan: Our SREs also want to run a small load test to see tail lat. Can Redwood coordinate?
[23:22] Owen: Yes — we can schedule a coordinated run, provide a staging endpoint and monitoring hooks.

[24:00] Priya: Any gotchas with vector DB connectors? We run Milvus and Pinecone today.
[24:06] Owen: We integrate with common vector DBs via standard size-agnostic vectors. For Pinecone sometimes metadata shapes cause small extra latency; we have connector notes. For Milvus you're fine, just ensure float32 support.

[25:10] Maya: Okay let's recap — Maya to send pricing and example unit economics; Owen to send SOC2 + security whitepaper + network diagram; Redwood will run benchmark with Priya and produce initial ndcg/p95 report by 2026-01-20; schedule POC scoping call next week.

[26:00] Mark: Sounds good, is there a trial credit or sandbox?
[26:05] Maya: Yes we provide trial credits for hosted so you can run the 10k ingestion without charge while we scope. We'll allocate credits when you approve the POC scoping doc.

[27:10] Priya: Can you also share the Console screenshots of the rerank per-route breakdown? That helps our product folks.
[27:16] Samir: Absolutely will include in the follow-up deck — per-route latency, token breakdown and canary control images.

[28:30] Jenna: Any noted regs for EU export? Our customers are global.
[28:36] Owen: We'll include region controls; for strict residency we recommend Private or VPC deployments.

[30:00] (demo wrap up)
[30:12] Maya: Quick live Q&A?
[30:18] Mark: One more technical — how do you handle cold-start for a reranker with large KV cache misses?
[30:24] Owen: Cold start costs can spike; runtime keeps a warmed KV cache for hot model shards and does prefetching. If you expect many unique contexts we can tune cache TTLs.

[31:45] Priya: For the benchmark, do we need to mask PII? The sample has real tracking IDs.
[31:50] Maya: We prefer anonymized data but can run on masked data or sign an NDA. We'll coordinate with your legal.

[33:00] Ethan: We'll want a SLA on p99 for critical routes if we move to Dedicated.
[33:06] Maya: Yes Dedicated offers SLA-backed p99s and reserved capacity; we'll include the SLA terms in the follow-up.

[34:20] Jenna: Are there any known regressions when upgrading model versions in the reranker pipeline?
[34:26] Owen: Occasionally ranking shifts; that's why we do canaries and holdback evals. Console can auto-detect regressed prompts with eval sets.

[35:10] Priya: Can Optimize provide suggested quantization profile and expected NDCG loss?
[35:16] Owen: Optimize provides sim heuristics and could run a small fidelity test to estimate ndcg impact of quantization.

[36:00] Maya: Final admin items — I'll send invite for POC scoping next Tue 2026-01-13 16:00 UTC. Does that work?
[36:08] Jenna: Works for me.
[36:12] Mark: Works.

[37:30] (closing notes)
[38:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with pricing, security docs, and schedule the benchmark. Really appreciate your time.
[38:08] Jenna: Thanks.
[38:10] Mark: Thanks, bye.
[38:12] Priya: Thanks.

[41:00] (call ends)
